title: Keys — Import Wrapping Key — payload
description: Asks a key custodian for a fresh, short-lived, single-use public key to seal a private key to before sending it in a keys/import request's `privateKeySealed` carrier. The request carries nothing. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

Response.title: Keys — Import Wrapping Key — response payload
Response.description: The wrapping key the custodian has just generated, carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/keys/import-wrapping-key/0.1#response. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

wrappingKey.description: The wrapping key as an Ed25519 did:key. A producer seals to its X25519 counterpart (the birational map of RFC 7748 §4.1 applied to the Ed25519 public key), exactly as the sealed-transfer recipient of vta/attestation/mnemonic-export is addressed. Generated for this response alone: the custodian MUST NOT return the same key twice.

keyId.description: The custodian's opaque handle for this wrapping key. A `privateKeyJwe` carrier names it as its JWE `kid`. A `privateKeySealed` carrier does not need it: the custodian finds the key by trying the bundle against its unexpired, unused wrapping keys. Carries no meaning to the producer beyond equality.

expiresAt.description: The instant after which the custodian will no longer open anything sealed to this key. RFC 3339 with an explicit offset. A producer that cannot complete keys/import before it asks for a new wrapping key rather than sending a bundle it knows will be refused.
